prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your ZIP code, the size/condition of your home and ductwork, your brand preferences and budget. I can help you find the best option for your situation, but I’ll need a ZIP code and a few details to give tailored recommendations.

Meanwhile, here’s a short, practical guide so you can quickly find a top installer in Atlanta and avoid common pitfalls.

Quick shortlist (well-known, widely used in the Atlanta area)
- Coolray — large regional company with many Atlanta-area crews.
- R.S. Andrews — long-established Atlanta-based company.
- National franchise options (One Hour Heating & Air/Aire Serv/ARS) — widely available with standardized processes.

Use those names as a starting point, but also look for highly rated local independent contractors in your neighborhood — some independents provide excellent, personalized service and competitive pricing.

How to pick the best company (checklist)
- Licensing & insurance: Ask for GA HVAC license and proof of insurance.
- Certifications: NATE-certified technicians are a good sign.
- Load calculation: Insist on a Manual J load calculation (not just “match the old unit”).
- Written estimate: Get a detailed written quote showing equipment model, SEER rating, tonnage, line-set length, permits, labor, and any ductwork or electrical work.
- Permits & code: Company should obtain required permits and comply with local codes.
- Warranty: Confirm equipment manufacturer’s warranty and a minimum 1–2 year labor warranty from the contractor. Ask how warranty service is handled.
- References & reviews: Check Google, Yelp, BBB, and ask for recent local references.
- Installation quality: Ask about refrigerant charge procedure, duct sealing, and whether they perform a start-up checklist and provide operating instructions.
- Financing & rebates: Ask about financing and available utility or manufacturer rebates (Georgia Power and other utilities sometimes offer rebates for high-efficiency units).

Questions to ask every company
- Are you licensed and insured in Georgia? Can you provide proof?
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation? Can I see it?
- What exact make/model are you recommending, SEER rating, and why?
- What is included in the price (permit, disposal of old unit, thermostat, duct repair)?
- What warranties come with the equipment and labor?
- Can you provide 3 local references from similar-sized homes?
- Do you offer a written maintenance plan?

Typical cost range (Atlanta, ballpark)
- Small/entry-level replacement (single-story, 2–2.5 ton, basic brand): roughly $3,500–$6,000.
- Mid-range (3–4 ton, higher SEER, new condenser + coil): roughly $5,000–$9,000.
- High-efficiency / larger homes or ductwork replacement: $8,000–$15,000+.
(Prices vary by house size, brand, ductwork condition, and installation complexity. Get multiple quotes.)

Next step
If you want, give me:
- Your ZIP code
- Age/brand of existing system (if known)
- House size (sq ft) and number of levels
- Any brand or efficiency preference
- Budget or timeline constraints

I’ll find 3–4 top-rated installers in your area, summarize reviews, and give pros/cons so you can pick the best contractor to replace your AC.
